intro: This library is reviewed against primary sources, not secondary summaries. 12 changes in the last ninety days, from the state bill tracker, the federal agency watch and the framework explainers, newest first.

items.body: We compared the enrolled text of the AI measures states have passed. States regulate uses, not the technology. The most common duty is disclosure, a human must make the high stakes call, and the attorney general enforces.
items.headline: What State AI Laws Have in Common

items.body: The pre-existing control frameworks that layer beneath AI governance but do not substitute for it.
items.headline: General Business Governance

items.body: How the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act governs AI at financial institutions. Safeguards Rule, Privacy Rule, third-party oversight.
items.headline: GLBA and AI

items.body: FedRAMP is the General Services Administration program that sets one standard way to assess the security of cloud services for federal agencies. Its AI Prioritization Initiative ran from August 2025 to April 2026 and ended with three AI services certified. The program is now moving to FedRAMP 20x.
items.headline: FedRAMP and AI

items.body: How the Fair Credit Reporting Act governs AI that produces consumer reports. Accuracy, adverse action notices, dispute rights.
items.headline: FCRA and AI

items.body: An AI system that stores, processes or transmits payment card data is in scope for PCI DSS like any other technology. The PCI Security Standards Council has published AI principles, assessment guidelines and, on September 15, 2026, an information supplement on the security of AI systems. All three are guidance, and the standard itself takes precedence.
items.headline: PCI DSS and AI

items.body: The EDM Council's capability model for measuring data management maturity, widely used in financial services.
items.headline: EDM Council DCAM

items.body: How the Equal Credit Opportunity Act governs AI in lending: adverse action notices, specific reasons, and what the 2026 Regulation B rule changed on disparate impact.
items.headline: ECOA and AI

items.body: HITRUST CSF is a certifiable security framework from HITRUST, a private standards body. It underlies three certifications, e1, i1 and r2, and since late 2024 an AI Security Certification for deployed AI systems. It is not a law and HIPAA does not require it.
items.headline: HITRUST CSF

items.body: Under GLBA a lender stays responsible for customer data it gives an AI vendor. The Safeguards Rule requires vendor selection, contract safeguards and ongoing assessment, and the Privacy Rule limits the vendor to the purpose the data was shared for.
items.headline: AI Vendor Due Diligence Under GLBA

items.body: ST. GEORGE , Utah – A Washington County man was sentenced to 60 months’ imprisonment after law enforcement found child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on his phone, which had been digitally altered.
items.headline: DOJ: Washington County Man Sentenced to Five Years’ Imprisonment for Possession of Sexually Explicit AI Photos of Children

items.body: Michael A. Huseman possessed over 22,000 files containing child sexual abuse material (CSAM), 6,000 anime files depicting children being sexually abused and over 400 files of AI-generated CSAM.
items.headline: DOJ: Missouri Man Who Possessed AI-Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material Sentenced to 14 Years in Prison
